1.visual: A bold downward-pointing arrow with a straight vertical shaft and a wide triangular arrowhead at the bottom. The stroke is thick and the arrowhead has flat horizontal ends on each side, giving it a T-bar quality.
1.usage: Scroll down prompts, download buttons, collapse/expand sections downward, sorting indicator for descending order.

2.visual: A bold leftward-pointing arrow with a straight horizontal shaft and a wide triangular arrowhead on the left side. Stroke weight matches icon 1 but the arrowhead terminates with flat vertical ends top and bottom.
2.usage: Back navigation button, previous page in pagination, undo/go back in multi-step flows, carousel previous slide.

3.visual: Two horizontal arrows pointing in opposite directions: one pointing left on top and one pointing right below it, both with filled arrowheads. The pair is stacked vertically and suggests bidirectional movement.
3.usage: Transfer or swap between two items, compare mode toggle, bidirectional data sync, currency or unit conversion input.

4.visual: A bold rightward-pointing arrow with a straight horizontal shaft and a wide triangular arrowhead on the right. Visually mirrors icon 2 but facing right; same thick stroke weight.
4.usage: Forward navigation, next page in pagination, proceed to next step in a wizard, carousel next slide.

5.visual: A bold upward-pointing arrow with a straight vertical shaft and a wide triangular arrowhead at the top. Visually mirrors icon 1 but facing up; same thick stroke and T-bar arrowhead style.
5.usage: Scroll to top, upload action, increase/ascending sort indicator, expand section upward.

6.visual: Two arrows stacked vertically: one pointing up on the left and one pointing down on the right, with both arrowheads filled. The pair suggests bidirectional vertical movement or sorting.
6.usage: Sort column toggle (ascending/descending), drag-to-reorder handle, vertical scroll indicator, swap order of items.

7.visual: A thin chevron (V-shape) pointing downward, drawn with two short diagonal strokes meeting at a point at the bottom. No shaft — just the angled chevron shape, lighter weight than the bold arrow in icon 1.
7.usage: Expand accordion or dropdown, show more content below, select/combo box open indicator, collapsible section trigger.

8.visual: A thin chevron pointing left with a vertical bar (pipe) immediately to its left. The chevron is a single open angle, and the vertical bar acts as a boundary stop, together forming a skip-to-start symbol.
8.usage: Skip to first page in pagination, rewind to beginning of media, jump to start of a list or sequence.

9.visual: A thin chevron pointing right with a vertical bar (pipe) immediately to its right. Mirrors icon 8; the chevron and stop bar form a skip-to-end symbol.
9.usage: Skip to last page in pagination, fast-forward to end of media, jump to end of a list or sequence.

10.visual: A thin single chevron pointing left, drawn as two diagonal strokes meeting at a leftward point with no shaft or bar. Lighter and smaller visual weight than the bold arrow in icon 2.
10.usage: Previous page in pagination, collapse sidebar, go back one step, carousel previous (minimal style).

11.visual: A thin single chevron pointing right, drawn as two diagonal strokes meeting at a rightward point. Mirrors icon 10; no shaft or bar, lighter weight than the bold arrow in icon 4.
11.usage: Next page in pagination, expand sidebar, go forward one step, carousel next (minimal style).

12.visual: A thin chevron pointing upward, drawn as two diagonal strokes meeting at a top point. Mirrors icon 7 but rotated 180 degrees; same lightweight open V shape.
12.usage: Collapse accordion or section, scroll up indicator, close dropdown/menu, step back in vertical flow.

13.visual: Two thin chevrons stacked vertically and pointing toward each other — one pointing down on top and one pointing up below — creating a compressed or pinch symbol.
13.usage: Collapse expanded content, minimize vertical space, close a vertically expanded panel, compress list view.

14.visual: Two thin chevrons placed side by side horizontally and pointing away from each other — one pointing left on the left and one pointing right on the right — suggesting horizontal expansion.
14.usage: Expand panel horizontally, resize splitter, code view toggle, separate two columns or panes.

15.visual: Two thin chevrons stacked vertically and pointing away from each other — one pointing up on top and one pointing down below — suggesting vertical expansion or a sort selector.
15.usage: Expand content vertically, sortable column header indicator, resize handle, number input spinner control.

16.visual: A circle outline containing a small filled diamond (rotated square) at its center. The compass-rose shape of the diamond inside the ring gives this a directional exploration feel.
16.usage: Compass or explore/discover navigation, browser address bar, map orientation, app explore tab.

17.visual: A bent arrow that travels rightward then curves downward and left, forming an L-shaped return path with a leftward arrowhead at the end. Represents a reply or return action.
17.usage: Reply to message, return/enter key affordance, go back after navigating forward, undo last action.

18.visual: A bent arrow that travels rightward from a lower-left origin, curves up and right along an L-shape, with a rightward arrowhead at the end. Represents a forward redirect or sub-item indentation.
18.usage: Forward or redirect action, sub-item or nested reply indicator, indented thread continuation, 'send to' or share forward.

19.visual: A circle outline with four small tick marks at the top, bottom, left, and right positions (like compass points), forming a crosshair or targeting reticle inside the ring.
19.usage: Current location / GPS target, focus on map position, crosshair for precision selection, center viewport action.

20.visual: A square with an open corner at the top-right, with an arrow pointing diagonally outward toward the upper-right from inside the square. Represents opening content in a new tab or external window.
20.usage: Open link in new tab, external link indicator, launch in new window, view full page from embedded preview.

21.visual: A house outline with a triangular pitched roof, a rectangular base, and a small rectangular door cutout at the bottom center. Clean, minimal stroke with no fill.
21.usage: Home/dashboard navigation link, return to homepage, breadcrumb root, main menu home button.

22.visual: A layout grid showing one tall narrow rectangle on the left spanning the full height, and two smaller squares stacked on the right side. Represents a sidebar-left with content panel layout.
22.usage: Toggle sidebar layout, switch to panel view, dashboard layout selector, enable left-nav layout mode.

23.visual: A layout grid showing one wide rectangle spanning the full top, and two smaller squares side-by-side in the bottom row. Represents a top header with two-column content layout.
23.usage: Switch to header-plus-columns layout, dashboard layout selector, page template chooser, content arrangement toggle.

24.visual: Three horizontal parallel lines of equal length and equal spacing, stacked vertically. Classic hamburger menu symbol with no additional decoration.
24.usage: Toggle mobile navigation drawer, open sidebar menu, expand hidden navigation options, app menu button.

25.visual: A filled arrow cursor pointing toward the upper-left, shaped like a traditional mouse pointer with a sharp tip at the top-left and a notched tail. The cursor is solid black with a slight angular cutout at the bottom-right of the body.
25.usage: Cursor / pointer mode selector in drawing or design tools, indicate interactive/clickable state, select tool in an editor, mouse input mode indicator.
